title: 4 days Ultra Minimalistic Upper Lower program review
summary: NH reviews a viewer's 4-day upper/lower program built on 3x3 strength work followed by repeated back-off sets of the same lifts. He praises the 3x3 openers but criticises the minimalistic repetition of the same movements, junk volume on leg press, lack of knee-flexion/hip-hinge balance, and missing body parts, proposing variations, supersets and giant sets instead.
claims: He organises upper/lower days around a main movement pattern and body-part focus (e.g. a bench-focused upper day), which makes it effectively a body-part split he calls the Gentleman split
The classic 2-upper/2-lower template is a good consensus but people should not get stuck in it; frequency can go to 5-6 days, add an arm day, or convert to a Gentleman split
Gentleman-style splits make adding tonnage and training every muscle group much easier than a plain upper/lower
3x3 is one of his favourite strength rep schemes because it leaves little room to sandbag and keeps intensity very high
3x3 works for bench, squat, pull-ups and is amazing for deadlift, but lacks the volume he wants for the overhead press
Accessory/tonnage lifts such as rows or Romanian deadlifts should not be run as 3x3; 3x3 is for strength work and possibly back-off sets
Weighted pull-ups suit 3x3 strength work; bodyweight pull-ups should just be done for as many reps as possible
The more sets you do, the more time supersetting saves; supersetting two 3-set strength lifts only saves three short sets, so separating them is fine
A deferred back-off set (not right after the strength sets) lets you recover more but may require some re-warming
After a 3x3, a 3x8-12 back-off set on the same lift is a bit too much volume; use a variation such as Spoto press, close-grip or incline press instead
Paused bench for 8-12 reps does not fit the tempo and mentality of pause reps
Repeating the same compound movement eventually fails and invites tendonitis and overuse injuries; programming a variation in advance prevents this
Leaning-back sternum pull-ups turn the pull-up into more of a horizontal pull that hits the upper back harder
Using variations loses some specificity but gains raw progression and injury prevention
Pair the bench back-off variation with rows or curls, and the pull-up back-off variation with lateral raises and triceps extensions, to save time and build cardiovascular endurance
Isolation lifts that hit different muscles (high rows, lateral raises, triceps extensions, curls) can be combined into one giant set without hurting performance
He prioritises hamstrings over quads, so only one of his four lower days is knee-flexion based; the rest are hip hinges
Opening with paused squats limits progression because you are weaker on paused reps; train the normal stretch-reflex squat first
Any lift with a similar movement pattern and stance still feeds the main lift, so you don't need to repeat the exact lift for specificity
Paused squats are possibly the best pure knee-flexion variation for big legs and a bigger squat, but 8-12 reps to failure is masochistic; he recommends 4-8 reps for quads
If you can still do meaningful leg press work after squat 3x3 plus 3x8-12, you sandbagged the squats; 6 sets of leg press on top is junk volume
A knee-flexion lower day cannot be only knee flexion; like never having only horizontal presses, it creates imbalance
He developed knee issues from letting his quads take over and hammering them
Replace the leg press with 6 sets of lying leg curls at 8-12 reps to balance the quads
Hyperextensions to failure pair well with forearm isolation, shrugs and calf work on lower days
Repeating an identical minimalistic upper day twice a week is a plateau in the making; create a second upper type with different exercises and rep ranges
A program with no direct biceps, little long-head triceps, no forearm work and only vertical pulling will create weaknesses later
Deadlift 3x3 then 3x6 back-off then RDL 3x8-12 is too many hip hinges; drop the deadlift back-off and add a knee-flexion movement
Pre-fatiguing the hamstrings with leg curls before squatting can lead to form breakdown and injuries
RDLs are negative-focused and have an exceptionally low injury rate when done properly
Leg curls after deadlifts plus RDLs are unnecessary since the hamstrings should already be cooked
Hanging leg raises decompress the spine
Lower days can be minimalistic in big lifts because squats and deadlifts cover most muscle, which leaves room to add cable/isolation work there and save time
exercises: great opener for an upper day; strength work
3x3 when weighted; bodyweight for max reps
back-off variation instead of repeating flat bench
lean back, try to touch the sternum
more horizontal pull, more upper-back work
best pure knee-flexion variation but limits progression as an opener
junk volume after heavy squats; fits better after deadlift days
